analysis: CHANGELOG.md units are documentation only, with no security-relevant behavior changes. The security-relevant change is in coordinator/api/install.sh. It adds PROVIDER_CONFIG, PRODUCTION_COORD_URL, provider_websocket_url(), bind_provider_coordinator() (head lines ~297-346), a --bind-coordinator-test hook, and a call after binary install. For any non-production COORD_URL it rewrites the [coordinator] url in provider.toml via awk. The URL is not validated beyond an https:// or http:// prefix. This turns the installer-session-only COORD_URL, which T-040 notes can be Host-header derived, into persistent provider routing configuration. That affects the TB-002 provider token and the registration path. Cross-file items the next pass should check: how the coordinator substitutes __DARKBLOOM_COORD_URL__ when baseURL is unset, whether the provider's ProviderConfig.swift accepts ws:// or arbitrary hosts, and whether sync-install-embed.sh keeps the embedded copy identical. The --bind-coordinator-test hook is only reachable by running the script locally. I could not verify the coordinator-side substitution because that source was not supplied.

findings.detail: The new bind_provider_coordinator() writes whatever COORD_URL the installer was served with into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml as the provider's permanent WebSocket endpoint. Before this change, COORD_URL only affected the install session and the provider kept connecting to production. COORD_URL is substituted by the coordinator, and T-040 says that substitution can fall back to the request Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers when baseURL is unset. A poisoned cache, a misconfigured proxy, or a lookalike host would therefore make an install permanently redirect the provider to a different coordinator. That coordinator would receive the provider token and the registration and attestation traffic, and could route traffic to the provider. The helper accepts `http://` and converts it to `ws://` (line 301), so a non-production coordinator gets a cleartext channel carrying the provider token. The value is also interpolated into awk and TOML with only a trailing-slash strip. It is not checked for quotes or backslashes, and awk -v interprets backslash escapes, so a crafted value can inject extra TOML content. The only protection is the production-URL string comparison. Fix: allow only https:// for non-localhost hosts, validate the URL against a strict hostname character set, and escape it before writing the TOML. Require explicit operator confirmation, or a signed or allowlisted dev domain, before overriding the default coordinator.
findings.title: Installer persists an unvalidated, possibly cleartext coordinator URL into provider.toml
